issues.failure_explanation: The claim that the L2-serendipity projection is 'solely determined' by the first N_S DoFs is asserted with no proof. In the generality of defvs it is false: the L2-projection onto S depends on the moments (v,p), p in S, which arbitrary DoFs need not determine. In the concrete face/edge/node constructions the property holds only under order conditions that are nowhere stated (face: k_r >= m-1 with original-space k_d = m-1; edge: mu_r >= m, beta_d >= m, k_d >= m-1 with original beta = m, beta_r = m-1; node: k_v >= m), and the assumed 'P^3_m-identifying' condition is strictly weaker: e.g. for the face space with m=1, k_r=-1 on a generic tetrahedron the kept DoFs [1],[2] already identify P^3_1, but a function w of the original space with zero kept DoFs (w.n=0, div w=0) can have nonzero moments (w, x-times-R), R in P^3_0, so the projection is not determined by the kept DoFs at these admissible parameters. The key equality Pi_m I^f_h v = Pi_m I^{Sf}_h v on which the proof of thmvf rests (the '=' step in prfvf), the analogous replacement in the proof of thmve, the computability of Pi^S on which the spaces' implementability depends, and the column-stability claim in thm:added-2 ('the existing columns of M^l do not change as l increases') all presuppose this unestablished property.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that \(\nabla v\in \mathbf{V}^{\mathrm{Se}}\ \forall v\in \mathbf{V}^{\mathrm{Sn}}, \nabla \times \boldsymbol{v}\in \mathbf{V}^{\mathrm{Sf}}\ \forall \boldsymbol{v}\in \mathbf{V}^{\mathrm{Se}}\), so \(\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_{l}\) should be acted on their entirety.

issues.failure_explanation: Diagram [2] requires that w = curl(I^{Se}v) belong to the serendipity face space, i.e. its reduced DoFs must match those of its own L2-projection Pi_{m''}. At a face-reduced order q with deg q <= mu_r this constraint reads (curl v, x-times-q) = (curl v, Pi_{m''}(x-times-q)) for all smooth v. Since a well-posed face space (determination, cf. ISSUE-001) forces reduced orders to satisfy deg q >= m'', the polynomial (I-Pi_{m''})(x-times-q) is nonzero and not a gradient, so taking v in C_c^infinity(int K) with (curl v, (I-Pi_{m''})(x-times-q)) != 0 (all boundary/trace terms then vanish, both sides reduce exactly to the moments of curl v) violates the constraint; hence curl(I^{Se}v) is not in V^{Sf} and diagram [2] fails. Equivalently, the construction would need curl-Pi_m = Pi_{m''}-curl identities that L2-projections do not satisfy; no parameter choice escapes (if all reduced orders lie below m'', the face space is exactly the ill-posed case of the determination issue). The same mechanism falsifies [3]: for v in C_c^infinity orthogonal to P_{m-1}, all kept edge-DoFs of grad(I^{Sn}v) vanish so Pi_m grad(I^{Sn}v) = 0, while (grad(I^{Sn}v), x_K h) = -(v, div(x_K h)) != 0 at reduced orders h of degree between m and min(k_f,k_v). Thus curl(V^{Se}) is not contained in V^{Sf} and grad(V^{Sn}) is not contained in V^{Se}. The given proof only verifies integration-by-parts identities for the standard spaces' DoFs and never checks the serendipity constraints (diagram [3] is moreover written with curl applied to the scalar-valued I^{Sn}v).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair preserving the L2-projection-based constraints was identified; at minimum, a repair must redesign the constraint mechanism (e.g. revert to DoF-based serendipity projections as in the cited prior work) or withdraw the commuting diagrams, the exact-sequence claims and the results depending on them.
issues.overall_effect: The serendipity de Rham sequence and commuting interpolants fail: the claims that curl v lies in V^{Sf} for v in V^{Se} and grad v in V^{Se} for v in V^{Sn} are false; thmve assertion [2] (and assertion [1], whose proof uses [2]) and thm:added-1 lose their proofs; the paper's applicability to curl/div problems and mixed formulations via the exact sequence is unfounded.
issues.title: Commuting diagrams [2] and [3] are false for the serendipity spaces (serendipity exact sequence broken)
issues.why_classification: A central structural guarantee is false under the paper's own design (L2-serendipity constraints); every resolution either replaces the construction with new proof architecture or abandons the commuting diagrams, the sequence-based applicability, thmve [2] and thm:added-1.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_{l}\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\|\) monotonically increases with \(l\), it must converges as \(l\rightarrow\infty\). Denote the limit by \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}\boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_{i}\right\|\). By the density of polynomials, \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}\boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_{i}\right\|=\left\|\boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_{i}\right\|\).
By the norm equivalence on a finite dimensional space, \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_{l}\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\|\approx\left\|\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\|\).

By \cite{daveigaInterpolationStabilityEstimates2022} (77,105), \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_{l}\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\|\le \left\|\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\|\le C_{K}\) for some polytope dependent constant \(C_{K}\).

issues.failure_explanation: The proof fails at several independent steps. (i) The limit objects psi^infty_i and Pi are undefined: no convergence of the varying Lagrange bases psi^l_i is established, and 'density of polynomials' applies to a fixed L2 function, not to the varying family psi^l_i, so the conclusion that the non-polynomial content of psi^l_i vanishes (norm equality at the limit) is unfounded. (ii) 'Since the Lagrange bases are linear independent, there must be some l making M^l full row rank' is a non sequitur: linear independence within each finite-dimensional V^S_l gives no uniform lower bound on the norm of a linear combination, which is exactly what is needed to rule out l-dependent degenerate coefficient vectors; this is the crux of the theorem and is not argued. (iii) The final 'norm equivalence on a finite dimensional space' yields constants with no uniformity, whereas the stabilization-free bilinear form a_h[u,v] = a_h(Pi_l u, Pi_l v) requires the two-sided bound with uniform constants. (iv) The bound on the serendipity basis functions cites standard-space interpolation estimates without justification. (The monotonicity/column-stability input itself additionally depends on the unproven determination property of ISSUE-001.)

failure_location.quote: Since the Lagrange bases are linear independent, there must be some \(l\) making \(\mathbf{M}^l\) full row rank.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish uniform stability of the serendipity Lagrange bases, prove that M^l has full row rank for some l (or otherwise the uniform two-sided bound), and control all constants uniformly in the mesh.
issues.overall_effect: The central stabilization-free guarantee - existence of an order l with a stable computable polynomial projection, on which the definition of the 'equivalent discrete bilinear form' and hence the whole stabilization-free method rests - is unproven; the paper's subsequent dimension-counting heuristics for choosing l are explicitly hedged ('most likely enough') and provide no substitute.
issues.title: Proof of the existence of a stable polynomial projection is logically invalid
issues.why_classification: The invalid steps constitute the core of the only proof offered for the paper's namesake guarantee; repairing them requires an essentially new argument not supported by the source, and without it the stabilization-free claim is unsubstantiated.
